ios.desc:
High Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) days are more common each year. This free Wet Bulb Tracker sends you alerts and keeps you informed. Plan your activities for the day, at work or with family, with your health and safety in mind.

Air Temperature is about hot air. Wet Bulb Temperature measures humid-heat conditions to indicate how much your body can cool without help, when active outdoors.

Our body runs at about 36°C / 97°F, so a Wet Bulb of 30°C / 86°F feels uncomfortably warm, and by 35°C / 95°F the body dangerously overheats.

THE OUTDOOR READING, FRONT AND CENTRE
Wet Bulb is usually read off instruments in the field, but mathematical models let us work it out from weather data for a location.

Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) is calculated in the app from air temperature, humidity, sun, and wind. Calculations follow the US National Weather Service's forecast method: a psychrometric solve for Wet Bulb, and the Dimiceli and Piltz globe model. This reading is useful when working, training, or walking outside, as a heat risk warning.

WET BULB MATH ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM 'FEELS LIKE'
Feels Like answers: how hot does the air feel?
A Feels Like of 32°C / 90°F is just a warm day.
Wet Bulb Globe answers: how much can sweating cool you outdoors?
A Wet Bulb Globe of 32°C / 90°F is Critical, and tells you to immediately stop exertion outside and stay actively cool. It matters.

HEAT ALERTS
Alerts notify you when outdoor Wet Bulb rises at your location. Adjust alerts in Settings.

SEE A WHOLE DAY'S TIMELINE
View an hourly timeline of each day's Wet Bulb Globe temperature, colored by safety level, showing how humid-heat builds and fades. Drag the marker across the day and the readings above it change. Hours likely to see rain show a smaller bar giving the percentage chance in your area.

KNOW WHAT TO DO
Every risk level comes with basic but handy Guidance: how long it's reasonable to stay out, what to watch for, and when to take breaks. The About page links to the Wet Bulb thresholds used by militaries, occupational safety bodies, and national weather services worldwide.

WORK IT OUT - GET AN UNDERSTANDING
The Calc tab lets you slide in any air temperature, humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation and watch both readings respond. Useful for teaching the concept or calculating from data.

FREE WET BULB TRACKER: The Wet Bulb Globe reading wherever you are, today's full hourly timeline with chance of rain, 'Rising Wet Bulb' alerts, Heat care guidance

quotes.text:
HN users may mostly know Wet Bulb Temperatures through Chapter 1 of 'Ministry for the Future' set in India. Well, the topic was close to home, so I built something for myself.

Where I live, the difficult dry summer heat usually peaked in May/June, but now seems to extend into September.

I grew up with 100F / 37C summers, sometimes reaching 110F / 43C, and temperatures around 86F / 30C felt familiar and manageable.
So it’s confusing when the same 86F / 30C now feels so much warmer.

May/June were hot but dry, so sweat didn't pool and stick... Now Jul through Sep the air often feels muggy, thick like a soup with moisture, holding heat well into the evening.

Thats really when it clicked for me what  WBGT/Wet-Bulb Temperatures was about:
Wet Bulb Temperature is not really a measure of 'hot' air like Heat Index. It’s a measure of how 'cool' my body can get by sweating.

Both are temperatures, but from different math, about very different things, and sending very different signals.

To make the signal more usable, I built *Wet Bulb Tracker*, an app that sends you automatic Notifications when wet-bulb conditions reach higher-risk levels, while telling you what the temperature risk level means. It’s to give the average home user a heads up.

I spent a lot of time iterating on the UI in Figma, trying to make WBGT look and feel more directly and immediately related to health, less like another Temperature. And to make it understandable at a glance.
